extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (USPTO agents and attorneys); USPTO enrollment & discipline stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing the conduct of registered patent practitioners before the USPTO, including duties when preparing/filing patent prosecution papers, signature/authenticity obligations, petition-to-revive requirements, and possible disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances (37 C.F.R. § 10.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner has a duty under 37 C.F.R. § 10.18 to conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances before signing and filing papers; the Final Order states Respondent did not fulfill that duty concerning why only two of the three inventors had signed the combined declaration and power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the practitioner had conducted a reasonable inquiry he could have uncovered the fraud (the third inventor was deceased) during prosecution and alerted the USPTO. Failure to make such inquiry may support disciplinary charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined Declaration and Power of Attorney must identify and be signed by all inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Combined Declaration and Power of Attorney accompanying a petition/filing must identify all inventors and be signed by them; the document filed by Respondent 'identified only Kesil and Gershenzon as inventors, and only Kesil and Gershenzon signed it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO may refuse to accept a power of attorney signed by fewer than all inventors (see USPTO decision refusing to accept power of attorney because it had been signed by only two of the three inventors). Ensure declarations accurately list inventors and obtain all necessary inventor signatures before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not handle a legal matter without preparation adequate in the circumstances (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must have preparation adequate in the circumstances before handling legal matters; Respondent acknowledged conduct violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b) by signing and filing papers without fulfilling his duty to inquire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate preparation includes reviewing documents for anomalies (e.g., missing inventor signatures, indications of death) and confirming supporting facts before filing that may affect the application's prosecution or validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice; Respondent's conduct was found to violate 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing or permitting filings that contain false or forged information, or failing to take reasonable steps to detect and correct such problems, can constitute conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice and lead to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of signatures and filings; forged signatures can give rise to inequitable conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents in prosecution must bear authentic signatures; the Final Order documents two instances where Margulis's purported signature was forged on USPTO filings and notes that the '287 patent was declared unenforceable due to inequitable conduct based on Margulis's forged signatures.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forged signatures on prosecution filings may lead to a district court finding of inequitable conduct and render a patent unenforceable. Practitioners should verify signature authenticity and investigate suspected forgeries promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Petition for Revival (37 C.F.R. § 1.137(b)) and accompanying materials
rubrics_metrics.description: A Petition for Revival of an application abandoned unintentionally under 37 C.F.R. § 1.137(b) must be properly prepared and accompanied by required forms and materials (petition for revival, transmittal fee form, cover letter, formal drawings, declarations/power of attorney as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an incomplete or incorrect petition package (for example, a combined declaration/power of attorney missing an inventor) can lead to USPTO not accepting parts of the submission or create downstream problems. Confirm completeness and correctness before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee/Notice of Allowance deadline and abandonment consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: When the USPTO mails a 'Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due' the issue fee must be paid within three months or the application shall be regarded as abandoned (as shown by the mailed Notice of Abandonment after non-payment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor deadlines tied to Notices of Allowance and pay required fees timely; failure to pay the issue fee within the statutory/office timeframe leads to abandonment and may require a revival petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and sanctions for practitioner misconduct (public reprimand, publication, notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions for violating USPTO disciplinary rules can include a public reprimand, publication of the Final Order and a Notice in the Official Gazette, OED filing a motion to dismiss pending proceedings, and OED giving notice of public discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary resolutions may require publication of the practitioner's misconduct and formal notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts where the practitioner is admitted. Parties generally bear their own costs as specified in settlement terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction and procedural bases for discipline (statutory and regulatory citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner discipline pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3), 11.26 and 11.59, and disciplinary proceedings must satisfy applicable regulatory procedures (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 settlement requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary proceedings and settlement agreements must comply with referenced statutes and regulations; practitioners should be aware of the procedural framework governing discipline before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing accuracy and completeness obligations for prosecution responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to Office Actions and other prosecution submissions must accurately identify inventors and contain truthful, complete information; the June 4, 2003 response bore a forged signature and incorrectly represented inventorship documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before filing responses to Office Actions or other submissions, verify the accuracy of signatures, inventorship statements, and supporting facts; incorrect or fraudulent filings can have serious consequences, including unenforceability and discipline.
